title: Permission and Preparations
reader_question: How did the long wait for permission end, and how were the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr made ready to leave?

overview.text: After the pledges at al-‘Aqabah, the Muslims of Makkah set out for Madinah in small groups, to brothers and a home where they would be safe. The Prophet ﷺ stayed behind, waiting for Allah's permission to follow them. Abu Bakr was ready to go too, but the Prophet ﷺ asked him to wait, hinting that he might not travel alone. So Abu Bakr waited, and while he waited he fed two riding camels. Then one day, at an hour when no one expected a visitor, the Prophet ﷺ came to his door.

paragraphs.text: When the Prophet ﷺ sent the Muslims of Makkah ahead, he had told them what the place was like: "I have been shown the land you will emigrate to, a land of palm trees between two lava fields." They left in small groups, and most of those who had once emigrated to Abyssinia came back and went on to Madinah as well.

paragraphs.text: Abu Bakr asked him again and again for permission to emigrate. Each time the answer was the same: "Do not hurry. Perhaps Allah will give you a companion." And each time Abu Bakr hoped that the companion would be the Prophet ﷺ himself. Once he had made himself ready to go, and the Prophet ﷺ stopped him: "Take your time, for I hope to be given permission." "Do you really hope for that, may my father be your ransom?" Abu Bakr asked. "Yes."

paragraphs.text: So Abu Bakr held himself back, to travel with him. He was a man of means, and he bought two riding camels and kept them at his house. For four months he fed them on the leaves of the samur, a desert acacia, to have them ready for the day they would be needed.

One day ‘Aishah and her family were sitting in Abu Bakr's house in the full heat of noon when someone said to Abu Bakr, "Here is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with his head covered, at an hour when he never comes to us." "May my father and mother be his ransom," said Abu Bakr. "By Allah, only something important brings him at this hour."

paragraphs.text: The Prophet ﷺ asked to come in, and was let in. Abu Bakr moved back from his couch so that he could sit. Only Abu Bakr's two daughters were with him, ‘Aishah and Asma. "Send out those who are with you," the Prophet ﷺ said. "They are only my two daughters," Abu Bakr answered. "What is it, may my father and mother be your ransom?" "Allah has given me permission to leave, and to emigrate."

paragraphs.text: Then Abu Bakr turned to the camels he had waited with for so long. "Prophet of Allah, these are two riding camels I have kept ready for this." "Take one of them," he said. "At its price," the Prophet ﷺ answered.

paragraphs.text: The two needed someone who knew the desert roads well. They hired ‘Abdullah ibn Urayqit, of the tribe of Banu al-Dil, a khirrit, a guide skilled at finding the way. He was a sworn ally of the family of al-‘As ibn Wa'il of Quraysh, and he still followed the religion of Quraysh. Yet they trusted him. They handed their two camels over to him, and he kept and grazed them until the time they had set. They agreed where and when he would bring the camels back: at the cave of Thawr, after three nights, on the morning of the third. From there he would lead them by the coast road.

paragraphs.text: "By Allah, I can find nothing to tie them with except my waistband," Asma told her father. It was the band of cloth she wore around her waist. "Split it in two," Abu Bakr said. "Tie the waterskin with one piece and the food with the other." She did, and from that day she was known as Dhat al-Nitaqayn, "she of the two waistbands."

in_depth.title: Two tellings of the noon visit

paragraphs.text: The visit comes to us from ‘Aishah through ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, in two lines of transmission. In al-Zuhri's, recorded by al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ comes with his head covered, Abu Bakr answers "they are your family", the permission is "I have been given permission to leave", and Abu Bakr's offer of a camel ends with "At its price." In Ibn Ishaq's, which he heard from "someone I do not suspect" from ‘Urwah, ‘Aishah adds that the Prophet ﷺ normally came morning or evening, that she and Asma were the only ones present, and that Abu Bakr wept for joy; it has "my two daughters" and "Allah has given me permission to leave, and to emigrate." The story above draws on both, and gives each line where it is the only one to have it.

paragraphs.text: In al-Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ answers Abu Bakr's offer with two words: "At its price." Ibn Ishaq tells the exchange more fully, and later, at the moment Abu Bakr brought the camels to him and offered him the better one: "I do not ride a camel that is not mine." "Then it is yours." "No. What did you pay for it?" "Such and such." "I take it at that price." Neither report gives the amount.

Ibn Ishaq tells the exchange more fully, and later, at the moment Abu Bakr brought the camels to him and offered him the better one: "I do not ride a camel that is not mine." "Then it is yours." "No. What did you pay for it?" "Such and such." "I take it at that price."
Neither report gives the amount.

paragraphs.text: The reports describe Asma's waistband differently. In ‘Aishah's words, Asma cut a piece of her waistband and tied the mouth of the food bag with it, and was called "she of the waistband". In Asma's own words, she split it in two, for the waterskin and the food, and was called "she of the two waistbands". Al-Waqidi, recorded by Ibn Sa‘d, joins the two: one piece tied the bag and the other became a strap for the waterskin's mouth. Ibn Ishaq places the waistband later, when the travellers were setting out from the cave: Asma had brought the food but forgotten a strap, so she untied her waistband and hung the food with it. Ibn Hisham adds that scholars he heard called her "she of the two waistbands", because she hung the food with one half and wore the other. This telling follows Asma's own account, which places the waistband at the packing in her father's house.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: فَلَمَّا أَذِنَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لَهُ ﷺ فِي الْحَرْبِ، وَبَايَعَهُ هَذَا الْحَيُّ مِنْ الْأَنْصَارِ عَلَى الْإِسْلَامِ وَالنُّصْرَةِ لَهُ وَلِمَنْ اتَّبَعَهُ، وَأَوَى إلَيْهِمْ مِنْ الْمُسْلِمِينَ، أَمَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ أَصْحَابَهُ مِنْ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ، وَمَنْ مَعَهُ بِمَكَّةَ مِنْ الْمُسْلِمِينَ، بِالْخُرُوجِ إلَى الْمَدِينَةِ وَالْهِجْرَةِ إلَيْهَا، وَاللُّحُوقِ بِإِخْوَانِهِمْ مِنْ الْأَنْصَارِ، وَقَالَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ ﷿ قَدْ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ إخْوَانًا وَدَارًا تَأْمَنُونَ بِهَا. فَخَرَجُوا أَرْسَالًا [٢]، وَأَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ بِمَكَّةَ يَنْتَظِرُ أَنْ يَأْذَنَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ فِي الْخُرُوجِ مِنْ مَكَّةَ، وَالْهِجْرَةِ إلَى الْمَدِينَةِ.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق في رواية ابن هشام؛ المتكلم الداخلي مصرح به في النص

source_units.text_ar: وَالنَّبِيُّ ﷺ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِمَكَّةَ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ: إِنِّي أُرِيتُ دَارَ هِجْرَتِكُمْ، ذَاتَ نَخْلٍ بَيْنَ لَابَتَيْنِ وَهُمَا الْحَرَّتَانِ، فَهَاجَرَ مَنْ هَاجَرَ قِبَلَ الْمَدِينَةِ، وَرَجَعَ عَامَّةُ مَنْ كَانَ هَاجَرَ بِأَرْضِ الْحَبَشَةِ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ، وَتَجَهَّزَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ قِبَلَ الْمَدِينَةِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: عَلَى رِسْلِكَ، فَإِنِّي أَرْجُو أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لِي فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: وَهَلْ تَرْجُو ذَلِكَ بِأَبِي أَنْتَ؟ قَالَ: نَعَمْ فَحَبَسَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ نَفْسَهُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ لِيَصْحَبَهُ، وَعَلَفَ رَاحِلَتَيْنِ كَانَتَا عِنْدَهُ وَرَقَ السَّمُرِ، وَهُوَ الْخَبَطُ، أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ.
source_units.speaker_ar: عائشة في رواية الزهري عن عروة في صحيح البخاري
source_units.text: The Prophet ﷺ was then in Mecca. He said to the Muslims, “I have been shown the place of your migration, a place of palms between two stony lava tracts.” Those who migrated went toward Medina, and most of those who had migrated to Abyssinia returned to Medina. Abu Bakr also prepared to go to Medina, but the Messenger of God ﷺ said to him, “Take your time, for I hope to receive permission.” Abu Bakr said, “Do you hope for that? May my father be your ransom.” He said, “Yes.” So Abu Bakr held himself back to accompany the Messenger of God ﷺ and fed two riding animals he had leaves of the samur tree, which are called khabat, for four months.

source_units.text_ar: وَأَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ بِمَكَّةَ بَعْدَ أَصْحَابِهِ مِنْ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ يَنْتَظِرُ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَهُ فِي الْهِجْرَةِ، وَلَمْ يَتَخَلَّفْ مَعَهُ بِمَكَّةَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ إلَّا مَنْ حُبِسَ أَوْ فُتِنَ، إلَّا عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، وَأَبُو بَكْرِ بْنِ أَبِي قُحَافَةَ الصِّدِّيقُ ﵄، وَكَانَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ كَثِيرًا مَا يَسْتَأْذِنُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِي الْهِجْرَةِ، فَيَقُولُ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: لَا تَعْجَلْ لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلُ لَكَ صَاحِبًا، فَيَطْمَعُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ أَنْ يَكُونَهُ.
source_units.speaker_ar: متن سيرة ابن هشام؛ لا تسمية جديدة للمتكلم في هذا المقطع

source_units.text_ar: وَأَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ بِمَكَّةَ بَعْدَ أَصْحَابِهِ مِنْ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ يَنْتَظِرُ أَنْ يُؤْذَنَ لَهُ فِي الْهِجْرَةِ، وَلَمْ يَتَخَلَّفْ مَعَهُ بِمَكَّةَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ الْمُهَاجِرِينَ إلَّا مَنْ حُبِسَ أَوْ فُتِنَ، إلَّا عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ، وَأَبُو بَكْرِ بْنِ أَبِي قُحَافَةَ الصِّدِّيقُ ﵄، وَكَانَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ كَثِيرًا مَا يَسْتَأْذِنُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِي الْهِجْرَةِ،
source_units.text: The Messenger of God ﷺ remained in Mecca after his emigrant companions, waiting for permission to emigrate. No emigrant stayed behind with him in Mecca except those detained or subjected to persecution, apart from Ali ibn Abi Talib and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them both. Abu Bakr often sought the Messenger of God's ﷺ permission to emigrate.

source_units.text_ar: فَيَقُولُ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ:
source_units.text: The Messenger of God ﷺ would say to him:

source_units.text_ar: لَا تَعْجَلْ لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلُ لَكَ صَاحِبًا،
source_units.text: “Do not hurry. Perhaps God will provide you with a companion.”

source_units.text_ar: فَيَطْمَعُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ أَنْ يَكُونَهُ.
source_units.text: So Abu Bakr hoped that he would be that companion.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ شِهَابٍ: قَالَ عُرْوَةُ: قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ: فَبَيْنَمَا نَحْنُ يَوْمًا جُلُوسٌ فِي بَيْتِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ فِي نَحْرِ الظَّهِيرَةِ، قَالَ قَائِلٌ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ: هَذَا رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ مُتَقَنِّعًا، فِي سَاعَةٍ لَمْ يَكُنْ يَأْتِينَا فِيهَا، فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: فِدَاءٌ لَهُ أَبِي وَأُمِّي، وَاللهِ مَا جَاءَ بِهِ فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ إِلَّا أَمْرٌ. قَالَتْ: فَجَاءَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ فَاسْتَأْذَنَ فَأُذِنَ لَهُ فَدَخَلَ فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ: أَخْرِجْ مَنْ عِنْدَكَ فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: إِنَّمَا هُمْ أَهْلُكَ، بِأَبِي أَنْتَ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، قَالَ: فَإِنِّي قَدْ أُذِنَ لِي فِي الْخُرُوجِ فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: الصَّحَابَةُ بِأَبِي أَنْتَ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ؟ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: نَعَمْ قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: فَخُذْ بِأَبِي أَنْتَ يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ إِحْدَى رَاحِلَتَيَّ هَاتَيْنِ، قَالَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ: بِالثَّمَنِ
source_units.speaker_ar: عائشة في رواية الزهري عن عروة في صحيح البخاري
source_units.text: Ibn Shihab said: ‘Urwa said: ‘A’isha said: One day, while we were sitting in Abu Bakr’s house at the height of midday, someone said to Abu Bakr, “Here is the Messenger of God ﷺ, with his head covered, at an hour when he does not usually come to us.” Abu Bakr said, “May my father and mother be his ransom! By God, something important must have brought him at this hour.” She said: The Messenger of God ﷺ arrived and asked permission to enter; permission was given and he came in. The Prophet ﷺ said to Abu Bakr, “Send those with you out.” Abu Bakr said, “They are your family, may my father be your ransom, Messenger of God.” He said, “I have been given permission to depart.” Abu Bakr said, “To accompany you? May my father be your ransom, Messenger of God?” The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Yes.” Abu Bakr said, “Then take one of these two riding animals of mine, may my father be your ransom, Messenger of God.” The Messenger of God ﷺ replied, “At its price.”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: وَكَانَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ ﵁ رَجُلًا ذَا مَالٍ، فَكَانَ حَيْنَ اسْتَأْذَنَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِي الْهِجْرَةِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: لَا تَعْجَلْ، لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يَجِدُ لَكَ صَاحِبًا، قَدْ طَمِعَ بِأَنْ يَكُونَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ، إنَّمَا يَعْنِي نَفْسَهُ، حَيْنَ قَالَ لَهُ ذَلِكَ، فَابْتَاعَ رَاحِلَتَيْنِ، فَاحْتَبَسَهُمَا فِي دَارِهِ، يَعْلِفُهُمَا إعْدَادًا لِذَلِكَ.
source_units.text: Ibn Ishaq said: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was a man of means. When he asked the Messenger of God ﷺ for permission to migrate, the Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Do not hurry. Perhaps God will provide you a companion.” Abu Bakr hoped that the Messenger of God ﷺ meant himself by this. He bought two riding animals and kept them in his house, feeding them in preparation.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: فَحَدَّثَنِي مَنْ لَا أَتَّهِمُ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ أُمِّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ:
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق عن من لا أتهم عن عروة عن عائشة
source_units.text: Ibn Ishaq said: Someone whom I do not suspect told me, from ‘Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘A’isha, Mother of the Believers, that she said:

source_units.text_ar:
كَانَ لَا يُخْطِئُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بَيْتَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ أَحَدَ طَرَفَيْ النَّهَارِ، إمَّا بُكْرَةً، وَإِمَّا عَشِيَّةً، حَتَّى إذَا كَانَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي أُذِنَ فِيهِ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِي الْهِجْرَةِ، وَالْخُرُوجِ مِنْ مَكَّةَ مِنْ بَيْنِ ظَهْرَيْ قَوْمِهِ، أَتَانَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ بِالْهَاجِرَةِ، فِي سَاعَةٍ كَانَ لَا يَأْتِي فِيهَا.
قَالَتْ: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، قَالَ: مَا جَاءَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ هَذِهِ السَّاعَةَ إلَّا لِأَمْرٍ حَدَثَ. قَالَتْ: فَلَمَّا دَخَلَ، تَأَخَّرَ لَهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ عَنْ سَرِيرِهِ، فَجَلَسَ رَسُولُ
source_units.text: The Messenger of God ﷺ never failed to come to Abu Bakr’s house at one end of the day, either morning or evening. But on the day he was given permission to migrate and leave Mecca from among his people, the Messenger of God ﷺ came to us at midday, at an hour when he did not usually come. When Abu Bakr saw him, he said, “The Messenger of God ﷺ would not have come at this hour unless something had happened.” When he entered, Abu Bakr moved back from his couch to make room, and the Messenger of

source_units.text_ar:
اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ إلَّا أَنَا وَأُخْتِي أَسَمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: أَخْرِجْ عَنِّي مَنْ عِنْدَكَ، فَقَالَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، إنَّمَا هُمَا ابْنَتَايَ [١]، وَمَا ذَاكَ؟ فِدَاكَ أَبِي وَأُمِّي! فَقَالَ: إنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَذِنَ لِي فِي الْخُرُوجِ وَالْهِجْرَةِ. قَالَتْ: فَقَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ: الصُّحْبَةَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، قَالَ: الصُّحْبَة.
قَالَت: فو الله مَا شَعُرْتُ قَطُّ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ أَنَّ أَحَدًا يَبْكِي مِنْ الْفَرَحِ، حَتَّى رَأَيْتُ أَبَا بَكْرٍ يَبْكِي يَوْمئِذٍ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: يَا نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ، إنَّ هَاتَيْنِ رَاحِلَتَانِ قَدْ كُنْتُ أَعْدَدْتهمَا لِهَذَا. فَاسْتَأْجَرَا عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ أَرْقَطِ- رَجُلًا مِنْ بَنِي الدُّئَلِ بْنِ بَكْرٍ، وَكَانَتْ أُمُّهُ امْرَأَةً مِنْ بَنِي سَهْمِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو، وَكَانَ مُشْرِكًا- يَدُلُّهُمَا عَلَى الطَّرِيقِ، فَدَفَعَا إلَيْهِ رَاحِلَتَيْهِمَا، فَكَانَتَا عِنْدَهُ يَرْعَاهُمَا لِمِيعَادِهِمَا.
source_units.text: God ﷺ sat down. Only my sister Asma bint Abi Bakr and I were with Abu Bakr. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, “Send away those with you.” Abu Bakr replied, “Messenger of God, they are only my two daughters [1]. What is it? May my father and mother be your ransom!” He said, “God has given me permission to depart and migrate.” Abu Bakr said, “Companionship, Messenger of God?” He said, “Companionship.” By God, before that day I had never realized someone could weep for joy, until I saw Abu Bakr weeping that day. Then he said, “Prophet of God, these are two riding animals I have prepared for this.” They hired ‘Abd Allah ibn Arqat, a man of Banu al-Du’il ibn Bakr whose mother was of Banu Sahm ibn ‘Amr and who was a polytheist, to guide them along the way. They entrusted their two mounts to him; he cared for them until their appointed time.

source_units.text_ar: وَاسْتَأْجَرَ رَسُولُ اللهِ ﷺ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ رَجُلًا مِنْ بَنِي الدِّيلِ، وَهُوَ مِنْ بَنِي عَبْدِ بْنِ عَدِيٍّ، هَادِيًا خِرِّيتًا، وَالْخِرِّيتُ الْمَاهِرُ بِالْهِدَايَةِ، قَدْ غَمَسَ حِلْفًا فِي آلِ الْعَاصِ بْنِ وَائِلٍ السَّهْمِيِّ، وَهُوَ عَلَى دِينِ كُفَّارِ قُرَيْشٍ، فَأَمِنَاهُ فَدَفَعَا إِلَيْهِ رَاحِلَتَيْهِمَا، وَوَاعَدَاهُ
source_units.speaker_ar: عائشة في رواية الزهري عن عروة في صحيح البخاري
source_units.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr hired a man from Banu al-Dil, who belonged to Banu Abd ibn Adi, as a khirrit guide—that is, one skilled at finding the way. He had entered into an alliance with the family of al-As ibn Wail al-Sahmi, and he followed the faith of Quraysh’s unbelievers. They trusted him, handed over their two riding camels to him, and made an appointment with him at

source_units.text_ar: غَارَ ثَوْرٍ بَعْدَ ثَلَاثِ لَيَالٍ، بِرَاحِلَتَيْهِمَا صُبْحَ ثَلَاثٍ، وَانْطَلَقَ مَعَهُمَا عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ، وَالدَّلِيلُ، فَأَخَذَ بِهِمْ طَرِيقَ السَّوَاحِلِ.»
source_units.text: the Cave of Thawr after three nights, to bring their two riding camels on the morning of the third. Amir ibn Fuhayrah and the guide set out with them, and the guide took them along the coastal route.”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ: فَجَهَّزْنَاهُمَا أَحَثَّ الْجَهَازِ، وَصَنَعْنَا لَهُمَا سُفْرَةً فِي جِرَابٍ، فَقَطَعَتْ أَسْمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ قِطْعَةً مِنْ نِطَاقِهَا، فَرَبَطَتْ بِهِ عَلَى فَمِ الْجِرَابِ، فَبِذَلِكَ سُمِّيَتْ ذَاتَ النِّطَاقِ،
source_units.speaker_ar: عائشة في رواية الزهري عن عروة في صحيح البخاري
source_units.text: ‘A’isha said: “We equipped them with all haste and prepared travel provisions for them in a bag. Asma bint Abi Bakr cut a piece from her waistband and tied it around the mouth of the bag; for this she was called ‘the woman of the waistband.’”

source_units.text_ar: «صَنَعْتُ سُفْرَةَ رَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ فِي بَيْتِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ حِينَ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُهَاجِرَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ قَالَتْ: فَلَمْ نَجِدْ لِسُفْرَتِهِ وَلَا لِسِقَائِهِ مَا نَرْبِطُهُمَا بِهِ فَقُلْتُ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ: وَاللهِ مَا أَجِدُ شَيْئًا أَرْبِطُ بِهِ إِلَّا نِطَاقِي قَالَ: فَشُقِّيهِ بِاثْنَيْنِ فَارْبِطِيهِ: بِوَاحِدٍ السِّقَاءَ وَبِالْآخَرِ السُّفْرَةَ فَفَعَلْتُ فَلِذَلِكَ سُمِّيَتْ ذَاتَ النِّطَاقَيْنِ.»
source_units.text: “I made the Messenger of God’s travel provisions ﷺ in Abu Bakr’s house when he intended to migrate to Medina. We could find nothing to tie his provisions and his waterskin with. I said to Abu Bakr, ‘By God, I cannot find anything to tie them with except my waistband.’ He said, ‘Split it in two: tie the waterskin with one piece and the provisions with the other.’ I did so, and for this I was called ‘the woman of the two waistbands.’”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: فَلَمَّا قَرَّبَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ، ﵁، الرَّاحِلَتَيْنِ إلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، قَدَّمَ لَهُ أَفَضْلَهُمَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ: ارْكَبْ، فِدَاكَ أَبِي وَأُمِّي،
source_units.text: Ibn Ishaq said: When Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, brought the two riding animals to the Messenger of God ﷺ, he offered him the better one and said, “Ride, may my father and mother be your ransom.”

source_units.text_ar:
فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: إنِّي لَا أَرْكَبُ بَعِيرًا لَيْسَ لِي، قَالَ: فَهِيَ لَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، بِأَبِي أَنْتَ وَأُمِّي، قَالَ: لَا، وَلَكِنْ مَا الثَّمَنُ الَّذِي ابْتَعْتهَا بِهِ؟ قَالَ:
كَذَا وَكَذَا، قَالَ: قَدْ أَخَذْتهَا بِهِ، قَالَ: هِيَ لَكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ [١] . فَرَكِبَا وَانْطَلَقَا وَأَرْدَفَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ ﵁ عَامِرَ بْنَ فُهَيْرَةَ مَوْلَاهُ خَلْفَهُ، لِيَخْدِمَهُمَا فِي الطَّرِيقِ.
source_units.text: The Messenger of God ﷺ replied, “I do not ride a camel that is not mine.” He said, “Then it is yours, Messenger of God, may my father and mother be your ransom.” He said, “No. What price did you buy it for?” He said, “Such and such.” He said, “I have taken it for that price.” He replied, “It is yours, Messenger of God [1].” They mounted and departed, and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, took his freedman ‘Amir ibn Fuhayra riding behind him to serve them on the road.

source_units.text_ar: قالت عائشة: وجهّزناهما أحبّ الجهاز، وصنعنا لهما سُفْرة في جِراب فقطعت أسماء بنت أبي بكر قطعة من نطاقها فَأوْكَت به الجراب، وقَطَعت أُخرى فصيّرته عِصامًا لفم القِرْبة، فبذلك سُمِّيَت ذات النطاقين.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن سعد عن محمد بن عمر الواقدي؛ الأسانيد المجموعة كما نص المصدر

source_units.text_ar: ومكثَ رسول الله، - ﷺ -، وأبو بكر في الغار ثلاث ليال، يبيت عندهما عبد الله بن أبي بكر، واستأجر أبو بكر رجلًا من بني الدِّيل هاديًا خِرِّيتًا (^١) يقال له عبد الله بن أرَيْقط، وهو على دين الكفر. ولكنّهما أمناه، فارتحلا ومعهما عامر بن فُهيرة، فأخذ بهم ابن أريقط يَدَ بَحْرٍ (^٢)، فما شعرت قريش أين وَجّه رسول الله، - ﷺ -.
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن سعد عن محمد بن عمر الواقدي؛ الأسانيد المجموعة كما نص المصدر

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: فَأَقَامَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ فِي الْغَارِ ثَلَاثًا وَمَعَهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ وَجَعَلَتْ قُرَيْشٌ فِيهِ حِين فقدوه مائَة نَاقَةٍ، لِمَنْ يَرُدُّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ. وَكَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ يَكُونُ فِي قُرَيْشٍ نَهَارَهُ مَعَهُمْ، يَسْمَعُ مَا يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِهِ، وَمَا يَقُولُونَ فِي شَأْنِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ وَأَبِي بَكْرٍ، ثُمَّ يَأْتِيهِمَا إذَا أَمْسَى فَيُخْبِرُهُمَا الْخَبَرَ. وَكَانَ عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ، مَوْلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ ﵁، يَرْعَى فِي رَعْيَانِ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ، فَإِذَا أَمْسَى أَرَاحَ عَلَيْهِمَا غَنَمَ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، فَاحْتَلَبَا وَذَبَحَا، فَإِذَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ غَدَا مِنْ عِنْدِهِمَا إلَى مَكَّةَ، اتَّبَعَ عَامِرُ بْنُ فُهَيْرَةَ أَثَرَهُ بِالْغَنَمِ حَتَّى يُعَفِّي عَلَيْهِ، حَتَّى إذَا مَضَتْ الثَّلَاثُ، وَسَكَنَ عَنْهُمَا النَّاسُ أَتَاهُمَا صَاحِبُهُمَا الَّذِي اسْتَأْجَرَاهُ بِبَعِيرَيْهِمَا وَبَعِيرٍ لَهُ، وَأَتَتْهُمَا أَسَمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ﵄ بِسُفْرَتِهِمَا، وَنَسِيَتْ أَنْ تَجْعَلَ لَهَا عِصَامًا فَلَمَّا ارْتَحَلَا ذَهَبَتْ لِتُعَلِّقَ السُّفْرَةَ، فَإِذَا لَيْسَ لَهَا عِصَامٌ، [١] فَتَحِلُّ نِطَاقَهَا فَتَجْعَلُهُ عِصَامًا، ثُمَّ عَلَّقَتْهَا بِهِ.
source_units.text: Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of God ﷺ stayed in the cave for three days with Abu Bakr. Quraysh offered a hundred she-camels to anyone who brought him back to them after he disappeared. ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr spent the daytime among Quraysh, hearing what they plotted and said about the Messenger of God ﷺ and Abu Bakr; at night he would go to them and give them the news. ‘Amir ibn Fuhayra, Abu Bakr’s freedman, tended livestock among the shepherds of Mecca. In the evening he drove Abu Bakr’s sheep to the two men, and they milked and slaughtered. When ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr left them for Mecca in the morning, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayra followed his tracks with the sheep to erase them. Once the three days had passed and the people ceased pursuing them, the man they had hired came to them with their two camels and one of his own. Asma bint Abi Bakr, may God be pleased with them both, brought them their travel provisions, but she had forgotten to provide a strap. When they prepared to set out, she went to hang up the provisions and found there was no strap [1]. She untied her waistband, made it into a strap, and hung them with it.

source_units.text_ar: فَكَانَ يُقَالُ لِأَسْمَاءِ بِنْتِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ: ذَاتُ النِّطَاقِ، لِذَلِكَ.
source_units.kind_ar: خاتمة تسمية في سرد ابن إسحاق
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق في نقل ابن هشام
source_units.text: For this, Asma bint Abi Bakr was called “the woman of the waistband.”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ: وَسَمِعْتُ غَيْرَ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُ: ذَاتُ النِّطَاقَيْنِ.
source_units.kind_ar: سماع من غير واحد غير مسمى
source_units.text: Ibn Hisham said: I have heard more than one scholar call her “the woman of the two waistbands.”

source_units.text_ar: وَتَفْسِيرُهُ: أَنَّهَا لَمَّا أَرَادَتْ أَنْ تُعَلِّقَ السُّفْرَةَ شَقَّتْ نِطَاقَهَا بِاثْنَيْنِ، فَعَلَّقَتْ السُّفْرَةَ بِوَاحِدٍ، وَانْتَطَقَتْ بِالْآخَرِ.
source_units.text: The explanation is that when she wanted to hang the provisions, she split her waistband in two, hung the provisions with one piece, and wore the other around her waist.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: قَالَتْ أَسْمَاءُ بِنْتُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ ﵄: فَلَمَّا سَمِعْنَا قَوْلَهُ، عَرَفْنَا حَيْثُ وَجْهُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَأَنَّ وَجْهَهُ إلَى الْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانُوا أَرْبَعَةً: رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقُ ﵁، وَعَامِرُ ابْن فُهَيْرَةَ مَوْلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ، وَعَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أَرْقَطَ دَلِيلُهُمَا.
source_units.kind_ar: خبر أسماء في نقل ابن إسحاق
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر
source_units.text: Ibn Ishaq said: Asma bint Abi Bakr, may God be pleased with them both, said: “When we heard his words, we knew which way the Messenger of God ﷺ was heading: toward Medina. They were four: the Messenger of God ﷺ, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, ‘Amir ibn Fuhayra, Abu Bakr’s freedman, and ‘Abd Allah ibn Arqat, their guide.”

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ هِشَامٍ: وَيُقَالُ: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أُرَيْقِطٍ.
source_units.text: Ibn Hisham said: It is also said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Urayqit.

source_units.text_ar: قَالَ ابْنُ إسْحَاقَ: فَحَدَّثَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ عَبَّادِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ أَنَّ أَبَاهُ عَبَّادًا حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ جَدَّتِهِ أَسْمَاءَ بِنْتِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ،
source_units.speaker_ar: ابن إسحاق عن يحيى بن عباد عن أبيه
source_units.text: Ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn ‘Abbad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr told me that his father ‘Abbad had told him from his grandmother Asma bint Abi Bakr:

source_units.text_ar:
قَالَتْ: لَمَّا خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ، وَخَرَجَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ مَعَهُ، احْتَمَلَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ مَالَهُ كُلَّهُ، وَمَعَهُ خَمْسَةُ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ أَوْ سِتَّةُ آلَافٍ، فَانْطَلَقَ بِهَا مَعَهُ. قَالَتْ: فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْنَا جَدِّي أَبُو قُحَافَةَ، وَقَدْ ذَهَبَ بَصَرُهُ، فَقَالَ: وَاَللَّهِ إنِّي لَا أَرَاهُ قَدْ فَجَعَكُمْ بِمَالِهِ مَعَ نَفْسِهِ. قَالَتْ: قُلْتُ:
كَلَّا يَا أَبَتِ! إنَّهُ قَدْ تَرَكَ لَنَا خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا. قَالَتْ: فَأَخَذْتُ أَحْجَارًا فَوَضَعْتهَا فِي كُوَّةٍ فِي الْبَيْتِ الَّذِي كَانَ أَبِي يَضَعُ مَالَهُ فِيهَا، ثُمَّ وَضَعْتُ عَلَيْهَا ثَوْبًا، ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُ بِيَدِهِ، فَقُلْتُ: يَا أَبَتِ، ضَعْ يَدَكَ عَلَى هَذَا الْمَالِ. قَالَتْ: فَوَضَعَ يَدَهُ عَلَيْهِ، فَقَالَ:
لَا بَأْسَ، إذَا كَانَ تَرَكَ لَكُمْ هَذَا فَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ، وَفِي هَذَا بَلَاغٌ لَكُمْ. وَلَا وَاَللَّهِ مَا تَرَكَ لَنَا شَيْئًا وَلَكِنِّي أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُسَكِّنَ الشَّيْخَ بِذَلِكَ.
source_units.kind_ar: خبر المال والحجارة وتفسير أسماء لقصدها
source_units.speaker_ar: أسماء بنت أبي بكر في الرواية
source_units.text: She said: When the Messenger of God ﷺ departed, with Abu Bakr alongside him, Abu Bakr took all his wealth; he had five thousand dirhams or six thousand with him, and took it along. My grandfather Abu Quhafa, whose sight had gone, came to us and said, “By God, I do not think he has hurt you by taking his money as well as himself.” [Translator’s note: the supplied text reads «إنِّي لَا أَرَاهُ»; the negation is unclear in this context.] I said, “No, father! He left us much good.” I took some stones, put them in a recess in the house where my father used to keep his money, and covered them with a cloth. I took his hand and said, “Father, place your hand on this money.” He placed his hand on it and said, “That is all right. If he has left you this, he has done well; this will be enough for you.” But, by God, he left us nothing. I only wanted to reassure the old man.

questions.prompt: How did the course of those Muslims who migrated differ from Abu Bakr’s position in ‘A’isha’s account?

options.text: Those who migrated did so; the Prophet ﷺ asked Abu Bakr to wait, and he held himself back in hope of accompanying him.
options.feedback: Yes: some Muslims began migrating while Abu Bakr waited to accompany him.

options.text: All the Muslims waited until Abu Bakr left first.
options.feedback: The text mentions the departure of some migrants before Abu Bakr remained behind waiting.

options.text: Abu Bakr prevented the Muslims from migrating until the Prophet ﷺ received permission.
options.feedback: The report says nothing of preventing others; only that Abu Bakr himself waited.

questions.explanation: The departure of some Muslims for Medina does not negate the Prophet’s waiting for permission ﷺ or Abu Bakr’s holding back to accompany him.

questions.prompt: What activity do the “four months” refer to in the account of the two mounts?

options.text: Abu Bakr feeding the two mounts samur leaves.
options.feedback: Correct: the duration follows the description of feeding them.

options.text: The journey from Mecca to Medina.
options.feedback: The report does not make it the journey’s length; it follows the feeding of the mounts.

options.text: Their stay in the cave.
options.feedback: This is the time spent feeding them before departure, not the stay in the cave.

questions.explanation: Observe where the duration appears: “he fed two riding animals ... for four months.”

questions.prompt: What made the Prophet’s arrival ﷺ at Abu Bakr’s house noteworthy in ‘A’isha’s account?

options.text: He came at the height of midday, at an hour when he did not usually visit them.
options.feedback: Correct: the unusual time is what marks the visit in the report.

options.text: He arrived with the two mounts at the door.
options.feedback: This passage does not say he brought the mounts.

options.text: He sent a messenger whom the report names instead of coming himself.
options.feedback: The person announced that the Prophet ﷺ was coming; the Prophet then asked permission to enter and came in.

questions.explanation: The description of the time and “at an hour when he did not come to us” explain why Abu Bakr inferred that something had prompted the visit.

questions.prompt: Who asked to accompany the other after permission to depart was announced, and what was the reply?

options.text: Abu Bakr asked and the Prophet ﷺ answered yes.
options.feedback: Correct: Abu Bakr asked and the Prophet ﷺ replied.

options.text: ‘A’isha asked, and Abu Bakr answered her yes.
options.feedback: ‘A’isha reports the conversation; she is not the person asking in it.

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ asked about companionship, and Abu Bakr declined.
options.feedback: In the text Abu Bakr asks and the reply is yes.

questions.explanation: The request for companionship comes between the announcement of permission and Abu Bakr’s offer of a mount.

questions.prompt: Who reports Abu Bakr’s tears of joy in Ibn Ishaq’s account in Ibn Hisham?

options.text: ‘A’isha, who says she saw him weeping that day.
options.feedback: Correct: the text attributes this observation to ‘A’isha.

options.text: Ibn Hisham, as an eyewitness present in Abu Bakr’s house.
options.feedback: Ibn Hisham transmits ‘A’isha’s account and does not describe himself as a witness to the visit.

options.text: The unnamed person who announced the Prophet’s arrival ﷺ.
options.feedback: That person appears in al-Bukhari’s account of the visit, not as the narrator of the tears here.

questions.explanation: The reading moves from Ibn Ishaq’s chain to ‘A’isha’s words, which identify who described the tears of joy.

questions.prompt: What does the price dialogue in Ibn Ishaq establish, without adding anything from outside it?

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ asked what the mount had cost and took it at that price; the amount is given only as “such and such.”
options.feedback: Yes: the dialogue establishes payment without specifying a number.

options.text: He accepted the mount as a gift without asking its price.
options.feedback: The text describes the offer as a gift, then its rejection and the question about price.

options.text: Abu Bakr gave an exact numerical amount preserved in the excerpt.
options.feedback: The reply preserved here is “such and such,” with no number.

questions.explanation: The answer “such and such” rules out supplying a specific amount, although the decision to take the mount for a price is clear.

questions.prompt: Which description preserves the difference between the two speakers’ pronouns in the preparation accounts?

options.text: ‘A’isha says “we equipped them” in the plural; Asma says “I made the provisions” in her own voice.
options.feedback: Correct: this preserves both the plural and Asma’s direct action.

options.text: ‘A’isha alone says “I made the provisions,” and Asma does not mention her work.
options.feedback: “I made” comes from Asma’s account; ‘A’isha’s uses the plural.

options.text: Both accounts attribute making the provisions solely to ‘A’isha in the singular.
options.feedback: Asma’s account uses the first-person singular; ‘A’isha’s uses the plural.

questions.explanation: ‘A’isha’s use of the plural does not mean she named every participant, and Asma’s own action does not erase that plural.

questions.prompt: What difference between ‘A’isha’s and Asma’s accounts of tying the waistband should we preserve?

options.text: ‘A’isha mentions a piece tied around the bag’s mouth; Asma mentions splitting the waistband to tie the waterskin and provisions.
options.feedback: Correct: the detail about the waterskin belongs to Asma’s account, not ‘A’isha’s excerpt.

options.text: ‘A’isha describes two pieces for the waterskin and provisions; Asma mentions only the bag’s mouth.
options.feedback: This reverses which account gives which details.

options.text: Both describe tying only the waterskin, with no provisions or bag.
options.feedback: Both readings address the provisions; Asma also specifies the waterskin.

questions.explanation: In ‘A’isha’s excerpt, “the woman of the waistband” accompanies a piece tied to the bag’s mouth; in Asma’s account, “the woman of the two waistbands” accompanies splitting it to tie two containers.

questions.prompt: In Ibn Hisham’s continuation of the provisions scene, where does his distinct voice appear, as opposed to Ibn Ishaq’s narrative?

options.text: In his statement that he heard more than one scholar say “the woman of the two waistbands,” followed by his explanation of splitting the waistband.
options.feedback: Correct: his comment follows the title at the end of the earlier narrative.

options.text: In Asma’s words “I made the provisions” as reported by al-Bukhari.
options.feedback: Those are Asma’s words in another reading, not Ibn Hisham’s comment.

options.text: In the sentence ending Ibn Ishaq’s narrative with “the woman of the waistband.”
options.feedback: That ends the narrative before Ibn Hisham’s comment.

questions.explanation: The reading separates the end of Ibn Ishaq’s narrative from “Ibn Hisham said” and the report and interpretation that follow.

questions.prompt: How does Asma explain placing stones where her father’s money might have been after his departure?

options.text: She wanted to soothe her worried grandfather and says her father left them nothing.
options.feedback: Correct: Asma ends by explaining her purpose.

options.text: The stones were money Abu Bakr left for her grandfather to spend.
options.feedback: Asma explicitly says they were stones and that her father left them nothing.

options.text: She wanted to prove that the amount was five thousand, not six.
options.feedback: The account wavers between five and six thousand; the stones do not prove either sum.

questions.explanation: Her initial words to her grandfather were meant to reassure him, not to prove that money remained in the recess; the uncertainty between the two sums remains.
